t.6.22.2: Having heard from his spies that the mighty Rāma had arrived, Rāvaṇa became somewhat agitated, and he spoke these words to his ministers.
t.6.22.1: Then, in Laṅkā, the king's spy reported that Rāghava, of unshakable strength, had encamped on Mount Suvela.
t.6.22.3: Let all the counsellors come quickly, fully composed and attentive, for, O Rākṣasas, the time for our deliberation seems to have arrived.
t.6.22.4: Hearing that command of his, the ministers came quickly. Then he took counsel together with his rākṣasa advisers.
t.6.22.5: Having taken counsel on what was fitting to be done next, that unassailable one dismissed his ministers and entered his own dwelling.
t.6.22.6: Then the great master of illusion summoned the mighty rākṣasa Vidyujjihva, a knower of illusions, and entered the place where Maithilī was.
t.6.22.7: And the lord of the rākṣasas said to Vidyujjihva, who was skilled in sorcery: "We shall delude Sītā, the daughter of Janaka, by means of illusion."
t.6.22.9: Thus addressed, the night-roaming Vidyujjihva said, "So be it." The king was pleased with him and gave him an ornament.
t.6.22.8: O night-wanderer, take a head of Rāghava made of illusion, along with a great bow and its arrows, and present yourself before me.
t.6.22.10: The mighty one entered the Aśoka grove, and there the younger brother of Dhanada beheld her, wretched though undeserving of wretchedness, her face cast down, wholly given to grief, seated upon the ground.
t.6.22.11: She who has gone to the Aśoka grove, meditating on her husband alone, attended close by by fearsome rākṣasīs.
t.6.22.12: Then, approaching Sītā joyfully and proclaiming his name, he spoke these bold words to the daughter of Janaka.
t.6.22.13: Though coaxed gently by me, O good lady, you still prance about proudly, relying on him: that husband of yours, Rāghava, the slayer of Khara, has been slain in battle.
t.6.22.14: Your root has been cut off on every side, and your pride has been struck down by me. Through your own misfortune, Sītā, you will become my wife.
t.6.22.15: O Sītā, you of little merit, whose purpose has come to nothing, foolish one who thinks herself wise, hear of the terrible slaying of your husband, like the slaying of Vṛtra.
t.6.22.16: Rāghava, it is said, has come to the shore of the ocean to slay me, surrounded by a mighty army led by the lord of the vānaras.
t.6.22.17: Having reached the southern shore of the ocean, Rāma encamped there with his mighty army as the sun was going to its setting.
t.6.22.18: Then, at midnight, the army, worn out by the march and halted, was sleeping soundly when the spies first approached it and reconnoitred it.
t.6.22.19: Then, by my mighty army led by Prahasta, his army was slain in the night, there where Rāma was together with Lakṣmaṇa.
t.6.22.20: Paṭṭasas, iron bars, swords, discuses, and great iron maces, showers of arrows, spears, and gleaming spiked hammers.
t.6.22.21: Raising them aloft again and again, the rākṣasas hurled staves, lances, darts, discuses and pestles down upon the monkeys.
t.6.22.22: Then, as Rāma lay asleep, his head was cut off cleanly with a great sword by the deft-handed Prahasta, the destroyer.
t.6.22.24: Sugrīva, lord of the monkeys, lies with his neck broken; Hanūmān, slain by the rākṣasas, lies with his jaw shattered.
t.6.22.23: Vibhīṣaṇa, having leapt up, was seized by chance, and Lakṣmaṇa, together with all the monkeys, has been driven off in every direction.
t.6.22.26: Mainda and Dvivida, both bulls among the vānaras, have been struck down; they lie sighing and weeping, drenched in blood.
t.6.22.25: Then Jāmbavān, as he sprang up on his knees, was struck down in battle, hacked by many spears, like a tree that has been felled.
t.6.22.28: Darīmukha lies in a cave, cut down by many iron arrows, while the mighty Kumuda, struck by shafts, lies there without a sound.
t.6.22.27: Struck by a sword and cut through the middle, Panasa, the destroyer of enemies, groans upon the earth like a jackfruit tree.
t.6.22.29: Aṅgada, set upon by many rākṣasas and cut down by their arrows, was struck down; spewing blood, Aṅgada fell upon the ground.
t.6.22.30: Monkeys were crushed by elephants, and others likewise by masses of chariots; there they were laid low and trampled, like clouds scattered by the force of the winds.
t.6.22.31: Others, terrified, fled, struck down from behind as they ran; pursued by the Rākṣasas, they were like great elephants chased by lions.
t.6.22.32: Some fell into the ocean, some took to the sky; and the bears, mingled with the monkeys, climbed up into the trees.
t.6.22.34: Thus your husband has been slain along with his army by my forces, and here is his head, brought to you, wet with blood and smeared with dust.
t.6.22.33: On the shores of the ocean, on the mountains and in the forests, many of those tawny-eyed ones were slain by the many with misshapen eyes.
t.6.22.35: Then Rāvaṇa, the supremely invincible lord of the rākṣasas, spoke these words to a rākṣasī while Sītā listened.
t.6.22.36: Bring here the rākṣasa Vidyujjihva, of cruel deeds, by whom that head of Rāghava was himself carried off from the battlefield.
t.6.22.37: Then Vidyujjihva, taking that head together with the bow, bowed his head in salutation and stood before Rāvaṇa.
t.6.22.38: Then King Rāvaṇa spoke to the rākṣasa Vidyujjihva, the great-tongued one, who stood there close beside him.
t.6.22.39: Quickly place the head of Dāśarathi before Sītā; let the wretched woman see well the final state of her husband.
t.6.22.40: Thus addressed, that rākṣasa placed that head, so handsome to behold, before Sītā and quickly vanished.
t.6.22.41: And Rāvaṇa too threw down a great, shining bow, renowned throughout the three worlds, and spoke these words to Sītā.
t.6.22.42: Here is that bow of your Rāma, fitted with its string, brought here by Prahasta after he slew that man in the night.
t.6.22.43: Then Rāvaṇa, together with Vidyujjihva, flung that head and the bow down upon the ground and said to the illustrious daughter of the king of Videha: “Be submissive to my will.”
